original_question: Consider the one-dimensional heavy-ball setting on F_{mu,L}, and let the purple region denote the set of tunings (gamma, beta) for which there exists a function in F_{mu,L} and an initialization whose heavy-ball trajectory forms a cycle. Can one prove that, in dimension 1, this full purple region of cycling tunings is actually achieved, thereby proving that heavy-ball cannot accelerate in dimension 1 either?
target_in_paper: Section 2 ("Open problem 1: behavior in dimension 1"), specifically the first of the paper’s "two connected conjectures": "Can we prove that the purple region representing all the cycles, is achieved in dimension 1, therefore proving that [HB] cannot accelerate in dimension 1 either?" ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2502.19916v1))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly targets the dimension-1 heavy-ball question over F_{μ,L}, it focuses on the purple cycling region rather than the broader Lyapunov/cycle gap of Open problem 2, and it preserves the paper’s intended implication: if the full purple region is attained already in dimension 1, then heavy-ball cannot accelerate there either. That is exactly the sharper Section 2 formulation sitting underneath the broader Section 1 question "Does heavy-ball accelerate over scalar functions of F_{μ,L}?" ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2502.19916v1))
missing_details: The scalar ambient space should be explicit: the paper’s question is about scalar functions, i.e. dimension d=1, so one is considering f: ℝ → ℝ and HB iterates x_t ∈ ℝ. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2502.19916v1))

The heavy-ball method itself should be written out as the two-step recursion x_{t+1}=x_t-γ f'(x_t)+β(x_t-x_{t-1}), since the paper frames everything in terms of this specific algorithm. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2502.19916v1))
F_{μ,L} should be defined stand-alone as the class of L-smooth, μ-strongly convex functions, with 0<μ<L. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2502.19916v1))

The phrase "purple region" should be tied to the paper’s actual usage: it is the region of tunings for which cycles are already known/proved on F_{μ,L} in dimension 2, and whose numerically found 1D counterpart is reported as indistinguishable in Figure 3. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2502.19916v1))

The existential quantifiers behind "achieved" should be made explicit: for each tuning (γ,β) in that region, one seeks some cycle length K≥2, some scalar function f∈F_{μ,L}, and some initialization of the two-step method whose HB orbit is exactly K-periodic. The paper’s definition of a cycle of length K supplies this quantifier pattern. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2502.19916v1))

The consequence "therefore proving that heavy-ball cannot accelerate in dimension 1 either" should be stated in the paper’s intended worst-case sense: Section 1 explains that the accelerated quadratic-tuning region lies inside the purple cycle region, so realizing that region in 1D would rule out acceleration over scalar F_{μ,L}. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2502.19916v1))

No homogeneity, polynomial degree, nilpotency, or other algebraic restrictions belong here; this paper’s problem is purely about real smooth strongly convex functions and heavy-ball dynamics, so those hypotheses should neither be added nor searched for. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.19916))
refined_question: Fix 0<μ<L, and consider the scalar Heavy-Ball method x_{t+1}=x_t-γ f'(x_t)+β(x_t-x_{t-1}) on functions f:ℝ→ℝ in F_{μ,L}, the class of L-smooth, μ-strongly convex functions. Let P_{purple}(μ,L) denote the purple cycle region from the paper, i.e. the set of tunings already known in dimension 2 to admit a heavy-ball cycle on some function in F_{μ,L}. Is it true that every tuning (γ,β)∈P_{purple}(μ,L) is also realized in dimension 1, in the sense that there exist an integer K≥2, a scalar function f∈F_{μ,L}, and an initialization of the Heavy-Ball method whose trajectory is exactly K-periodic? If so, this would establish that Heavy-Ball does not accelerate over scalar functions in F_{μ,L} either.
justification: The draft is aiming at the sharper Section 2 conjecture, not merely the broader introductory question. Section 1 first states Open problem 1 as "Does heavy-ball accelerate over scalar functions of F_{μ,L}?" and explains that the purple region consists of tunings for which cycles are provably found, with the acceleration-relevant quadratic tunings falling inside that region. Section 2 then reports numerical evidence that the 1D cycle region is indistinguishable from the known 2D purple region and culminates in the exact conjecture your draft is paraphrasing: proving that the whole purple region is achieved in dimension 1 would prove non-acceleration in dimension 1 as well. Finally, Section 3 provides the explicit quantifier structure needed to make the question stand-alone by defining what a cycle of length K means. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2502.19916v1))
